chunks: A number of our people have narrated from Sahl ibn Ziyad from Ibn Abi Nasr from Abd al-Karim from Abi Basir who said:

I asked Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him): Inform me about the words of Allah, Exalted and Glorious: 'And for the divorced women is provision in a fair manner, a right upon the pious.' What is the minimum of that provision if one is poor and cannot find much? He said: A scarf or similar things.

key_terms.بِالْمَعْرُوفِ: In a fair or customary manner
key_terms.مَتَاعٌ: Provision or gift given to a divorced woman
key_terms.مُعْسِراً: A person who is poor or lacks means

ai.seo_question: What is the minimum financial provision required for a divorced woman if the husband is poor?
ai.summary: In this narration from al-Kafi, Imam al-Baqir (AS) interprets the Quranic term 'matāʿ' (provision) by setting a tangible minimum for a divorced woman when the husband is indigent (mu'sir), identifying a simple headscarf (khimar) as sufficient. This establishes a practical legal baseline that balances the husband's financial hardship with the wife's right to dignified support, reflecting the Shia juristic principle of proportionality in family law.

en.sarwar: 5. A number of our people have narrated from Sahl ibn Ziyad from ibn abu Nasr from ‘Abd al-Karim from abu Nasr who has said the following: “

I once asked abu Ja’far, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, about the words of Allah, most Majestic, most Glorious, ‘. . . divorced women must be benefited with fairness. It is a right on the pious ones,’ and about what is the minimum of such benefits if one is not affluent. He (the Imam) said, ‘It is a scarf or similar things.’”
